quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. Other drivers need time to see your signal and prepare.

questions.question: On a highway in a motor vehicle, is it legal to have open alcohol containers?

options.text: No. You cannot drink from or have open alcohol containers in the passenger area.
Yes, if you are not the driver.
Yes, if the driver is not drunk.
No, you cannot drink from them, but you can transport open containers.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. You cannot drink from or have open alcohol containers in the passenger area.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink alcohol or have open alcohol containers in any vehicle on a highway. Open containers are not allowed in the passenger area of any vehicle on a highway.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: Suggested driving speeds for the area.
The fastest and slowest speeds you can legally drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest and slowest speeds you can legally drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum and minimum legal speeds. The maximum speed is for perfect conditions. You must slow down when weather or traffic conditions are bad.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid during winter.
Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip icy roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, or slippery roads. Winter driving is difficult and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and washer fluid levels. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare ahead without looking around. You stop noticing what is happening on the road, which can cause crashes.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you of railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and never try to drive around crossing gates.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Idling your car in the driveway.
Accelerating quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Sudden braking wastes gas because you must accelerate again. Look ahead and slow down gradually to avoid hard braking. This saves fuel and helps you drive more safely.

questions.question: On a road with two lanes going in opposite directions, which lane should you use?

options.text: Either lane.
The lane with less traffic.
The right lane, except when you are legally passing another vehicle.
The left lane if you plan to turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane, except when you are legally passing another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay on the right side of the road. Only use the left lane to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight.
You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
Wait for a solid green light before moving.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can drive only in that direction. The red light means you cannot drive any other way. Make sure the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided octagons. This unique shape tells drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats when they are too small for regular seat belts. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always make sure children are properly secured in a seat.

questions.question: Your vehicle is in an accident and is blocking traffic. You should:

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Never move your vehicle.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Stay at the scene and give your information to other drivers.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between you and other vehicles. This gives you enough time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: When driving in fog:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your low beams.
Use your high beams.
The type of lights you use does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the pavement. Use both hands on the wheel and make a small turn. Check for traffic before steering back onto the road.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. It is your responsibility to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be present ahead.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers you plan to change lanes. Watch for other drivers who may also be changing into the same lane.

questions.question: When driving at night, slow down and:

options.text: Use high beams when no cars are coming toward you.
Wear sunglasses to reduce glare from headlights.
Use high beams even when it is raining.
Use your dome light to see your speedometer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use high beams when no cars are coming toward you.
questions.explanation: You must turn on your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise. Use high beams whenever there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers are going too fast for the road conditions.
Drivers always check their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers give the right-of-way to others.
Drivers keep a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers are going too fast for the road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for current conditions. Always follow speed limits and slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: For a first driving under the influence conviction, if you refuse a breath test, your license will be suspended for at least:

options.text: 30 days
90 days
One year
Two years

questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: If this is your first DUI arrest in seven years, your license is suspended for 90 days. If you refuse to take a breath test on your first arrest, your license will be revoked for one year.

questions.question: A "No standing" sign means:

options.text: You cannot stop your vehicle there at any time.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly only to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly only to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and make sure no cars are coming.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder for your blind spot when passing left.
After passing, wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet before you change lanes. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until both headlights of the passed car appear in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.
